Clean concept values using config-defined plausibility ranges

Source: R/clean.R
clean_by_range.Rd

Flags (or drops / NA-sets) numeric values that fall outside the [min_value, max_value] window declared for each concept in the concept config CSV (rendehr_concepts_config.csv). This is physiology-based cleaning: bounds are fixed reference ranges, not derived from the data.

Usage

clean_by_range(
  df,
  ranges = NULL,
  config_path = NULL,
  src_name = NULL,
  value_col = "value",
  concept_col = "concept_name",
  single_concept = NULL,
  action = c("flag", "drop", "na")
)

Arguments

df

A data frame from fetch_concept()/fetch_concepts().

ranges

Optional override. A data frame with columns concept_name, min_value, max_value; or a named list of c(min, max) vectors. If NULL (default) bounds are read from the concept config CSV.

config_path

Path to the concept config CSV. Defaults to the bundled rendehr_concepts_config.csv. Ignored when ranges is supplied.

src_name

Optional source name; when given, config rows are filtered to that source family before building bounds.

value_col

Name of the numeric value column. Default "value".

concept_col

Name of the grouping column. Default "concept_name". If absent from df, all rows are treated as one concept named after single_concept.

single_concept

Concept name to assume when df has no concept_col (e.g. a single fetch_concept() result). Default NULL, which means: skip with a message unless ranges/config has a single row.

action

One of "flag" (add out_of_range logical column, default), "drop" (remove offending rows), or "na" (set offending values to NA).

Value

df with the action applied. A summary tibble (per concept: n, n_bad, min/max bound used) is attached as attr(result, "clean_report").

Details

When a concept has several config rows (e.g. one per source/table), the most permissive window is used: min(min_value) .. max(max_value). Concepts with no usable bound are left untouched (a message lists them).

Examples

hr <- data.frame(concept_name = "heart_rate", value = c(60, 300, -5))
ranges <- data.frame(concept_name = "heart_rate", min_value = 0, max_value = 250)
clean_by_range(hr, ranges = ranges)
#>   concept_name value out_of_range
#> 1   heart_rate    60        FALSE
#> 2   heart_rate   300         TRUE
#> 3   heart_rate    -5         TRUE
clean_by_range(hr, ranges = ranges, action = "na")
#>   concept_name value
#> 1   heart_rate    60
#> 2   heart_rate    NA
#> 3   heart_rate    NA
